High pressure weakening allowed increased cloud cover and thunderstorm potential, limiting insolation and capping afternoon temperatures near 32–34°C according to consensus model runs. This aligns with the observed moderation from earlier 35–38°C peaks, consistent with typical late-summer patterns when Atlantic influences suppress extremes. Traders are weighting official station measurements heavily, as any last-minute clearing could push readings toward 34°C while persistent clouds favor the 32°C bin. Updated guidance through the afternoon will refine these probabilities ahead of final resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus heavily favors a 28°C high in Seoul-Incheon on August 15, 2026, at 99.2% implied probability.** This reflects the moderating influence of persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and sea-breeze circulation from the Yellow Sea, which are expected to suppress daytime heating below the Korea Meteorological Administration’s 31°C forecast maximum.

Official short-range guidance notes 60% precipitation probability through the afternoon, with moderate easterly flow and convective activity limiting peak temperatures. Historical late-summer patterns in the region show similar setups frequently capping readings 2–3°C below clear-sky maxima, aligning with the market’s tight clustering around 28°C. Secondary outcomes such as 29°C hold only 0.5% odds, indicating limited model support for brief clearing that could allow additional insolation.

Realistic challenges to the dominant outcome include unexpected dissipation of cloud decks or reduced shower coverage, which could permit temperatures to edge toward 29–30°C. Sustained rain or thicker overcast would further reinforce the 28°C resolution threshold.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 16 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/es/madrid/LEMD.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from sources including the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and AEMET indicate Madrid will see a modest cooldown on August 16 after several days of 37–39 °C highs driven by strong high pressure. Ensemble guidance and local models converge on a daily maximum near 33–34 °C under partly cloudy skies with limited afternoon heating from scattered showers or increased boundary-layer moisture. Historical August climatology places the long-term average maximum around 32–33 °C, providing context for why traders have clustered implied probabilities on 34 °C (53.5 %) and 35 °C (35.5 %). Small shifts in cloud timing or frontal passage could still alter the peak by 1–2 °C before the observation window closes.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 16 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity is expected to maintain cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms over Metro Manila on August 16, moderating solar heating and suppressing peak temperatures below seasonal norms. PAGASA forecasts indicate a daily maximum near 29°C amid these conditions, consistent with recent observations of 28–30°C under similar monsoon patterns. The market's leading outcomes at 30°C (44%) and 31°C (24.5%) reflect trader consensus on partial clearing allowing modest warming, while lower probabilities for 32°C+ account for the low likelihood of significant monsoon weakening before resolution. Historical August averages near 31°C provide baseline context, but enhanced cloud cover and precipitation remain the dominant near-term controls.
